Demo 10: Mixer — Intelligent Audio Balancing (TF-0MLXF8ZW21HJLFOG)

Headline
Implement a behavior-aware Mixer runtime that enforces deterministic mix groups, priority-based ducking/boosting, and voice-limiting using declarative rules stored in repo JSON files.

Problem statement
Under concurrent audio/visual load (footsteps, combat, UI, ambience, etc.) outputs can mask each other and create an unusable, noisy mix. We need a deterministic runtime Mixer that applies intent-aware prioritization, ducking/boosting, and voice limits so the system maintains clarity and intent without human mixing.

Users
- Game/audio integrators and developers who embed ToneForge into interactive systems and need predictable, low-latency arbitration of concurrent outputs.
- Example user stories:
  - As a game audio engineer, I want ambience to be automatically ducked when combat activates so critical sounds remain audible.
  - As a developer, I want per-group voice limits so the system never exceeds allowed concurrent sources and avoids CPU spikes.
  - As an accessibility engineer, I want deterministic rules so we can reliably tune priority behavior and test outcomes.

Success criteria (measurable)
- Mix groups implemented and configurable: footsteps, UI, combat, ambience, dialogue, alerts.
- Voice limiting enforced per group with default max voices = 4; tests confirm group never exceeds limit under load.
- State-driven duck/boost rules applied from declarative JSON; default duck depth = 6 dB and UI duck duration = 200 ms.
- Max end-to-end mixer decision latency ≤ 5 ms under target load (benchmarked in CI test harness).
- `mixer` behavior is deterministic and unit-testable: same input state & events → identical rule outcomes and gains.

Constraints
- Depends on Runtime and State (Demo 9) being available for the Mixer to observe state and for Runtime to apply gain/limits.
- Must be low-latency and deterministic; avoid complex ML inference in the runtime path (Intelligence can suggest rules but must not auto-apply them).
- Rules storage must be auditable and version-controlled in the repository.

Existing state
- PRD: `docs/prd/MIXER_PRD.md` contains an extensive product-level design and examples.
- Roadmap: `docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md` includes Demo 10 context and example `mixer.inspect()` interactions.
- Worklog: TF-0MLXF8ZW21HJLFOG exists (title: "Demo 10: Mixer -- Intelligent Audio Balancing") and currently in `idea` stage, `open` status, assignee `Map`.

Desired change
- Implement core Mixer runtime features:
  - Mix group abstraction (intent-based groups)
  - Priority-based rule engine applying duck/boost/limit actions
  - Voice limiting enforcement per group
  - Deterministic rule evaluation with unit tests and fixtures
- Provide declarative rule schema and example JSON rules stored in `config/mixer/*.json`.

Related work
- Potentially related docs:
  - `docs/prd/MIXER_PRD.md` — full Mixer PRD describing concepts, examples, and goals.
  - `docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md` — demo sequence and Demo 10 scenario showing expected interactions.
  - `docs/prd/BRAINSTORM_QUESTIONS.md` — design tradeoffs and concerns about Mixer responsibilities.

- Potentially related work items:
  - Demo 10: Mixer -- Intelligent Audio Balancing (TF-0MLXF8ZW21HJLFOG) — current work item (idea, open, assignee Map).
  - Demo 13: Visualizer & Haptics -- Cross-Modal Output (TF-0MLXF9O241QG5APK) — lists Demo 10 as a prerequisite; cross-modal alignment may be relevant later.

Notes & open questions
- Rule storage path proposed: `config/mixer/*.json` (chosen to be versionable and human-editable). Confirm if another location is preferred.
- Scope: this work item covers the core runtime (mix groups, priority/rule engine, voice-limiting, deterministic evaluation). It intentionally excludes CLI/demo scripting and visual intensity control unless requested.

Draft created for review. Please review and either (A) approve, or (B) provide edits/answers to the short clarifying questions below.

Clarifying questions (pick or freeform)
1) Confirm the rules file path: `config/mixer/*.json`? (Yes / Different path)
2) Confirm mix group list: footsteps, UI, combat, ambience, dialogue, alerts? (Yes / Add/Remove)
3) Do you want me to add Demo 9 (Runtime & State) as a blocking dependency on the work item now, or should we leave dependency recording to a Producer? (Add now / Leave to Producer)

Risks & assumptions
- Risk: Scope creep — implementing cross‑modal visuals, CLI demos, or Intelligence auto‑apply could expand work beyond core runtime. Mitigation: record additional features as separate work items and keep this item focused on core runtime implementation.
- Risk: Runtime/State interfaces change during Demo 9 work, causing rework. Mitigation: lock an interface contract (API surface) in a short integration spike or use feature toggles; coordinate with Demo 9 owners.
- Risk: Real‑time performance targets are missed under heavy load. Mitigation: add microbenchmarks to CI and measure worst‑case latency; implement graceful degradation (looser voice limits) as a fallback.
- Assumption: Rules will be authored as declarative JSON and are sufficient to express required duck/boost/limit logic; more complex decision logic will be suggested by Intelligence but only applied after human review.

Polish
- The proposed canonical rules path is `config/mixer/*.json` (versionable and human-editable). Example rule schema and a small set of example rules should be added in the first implementation PR.

Final draft: please confirm or provide last edits. Once approved I will remove this temporary draft file and keep the work item updated.

Extend ToneForge beyond audio. The Visualizer generates deterministic, audio-synchronized visual effects. Haptics produces tactile feedback patterns. Palettes coordinate the aesthetic across all outputs.

As a game developer, I want ToneForge to generate synchronized visual effects and haptic feedback patterns alongside audio so that all sensory outputs are perceptually aligned and aesthetically coordinated through palettes.

Web demo with visual canvas:
```

  [Visual: cyan directional streak, 150ms]
  [Haptic: sharp pulse, 50ms, intensity=0.8]

  [Visual: subtle ground ripple, earth tones]
  [Haptic: soft thump, 30ms, intensity=0.4]
```

```bash
toneforge visualize export --recipe weapon-laser-zap --seed 42 --format spritesheet --frames 8 --output ./vfx/
```

- `toneforge visualize export --recipe <r> --seed <n> --format <f> --output <dir>`

1. Visualizer produces animated effects synchronized to audio events
2. Haptic patterns match audio intensity and timing
3. Palette changes visually and perceptually alter all outputs

Network, Integrations

**Network (two browser windows side by side):**
- Host broadcasts state changes to connected peers
- Client receives state changes and plays deterministically identical audio
- State transitions are synchronized across all connected clients

- Generate, validate, compile, and export sounds in automated pipelines
- Export for Unity/web with platform-appropriate file structure

2. Network bandwidth is under 1 KB/s for typical gameplay
3. CI pipeline validates, compiles, and exports without manual intervention
4. Unity/web export produces platform-appropriate file structure
5. Late-join clients receive state snapshot and sync correctly

# Problem statement

Add CLI subcommands `toneforge list sequences` and `toneforge list stacks` so sound designers and developers can quickly discover sequence and stack preset files from the command line, consistent with the existing `toneforge list recipes` command.

# Users

- **Sound designer**: Needs to browse available sequence/stack presets to find ones suitable for their game scenarios.
- **Developer**: Needs to script preset discovery (via `--json`) for build tools or workflow automation.

# User stories

1. As a sound designer, I want to run `toneforge list sequences` to see all available sequence presets with their names and descriptions, so I can pick one to audition.
2. As a sound designer, I want to run `toneforge list stacks` to see all available stack presets with their names and descriptions, so I can pick one to audition.
3. As a developer, I want to filter sequence/stack results with `--search` so I can quickly find presets matching a keyword.
4. As a developer, I want JSON output via `--json` so I can pipe results into build tools.

# Acceptance Criteria

1. Implement `toneforge list sequences` and `toneforge list stacks` — both scan the respective `presets/sequences/` and `presets/stacks/` directories, parse each JSON file to extract `name` and `description`, and display one line per preset in a table format.
2. Both commands support `--search <keyword>` that filters on `name` and `description` (case-insensitive match), consistent with `toneforge list recipes --search`.
3. Both commands support `--json` output returning `{ command: "list", resource: "sequences"|"stacks", total, presets: [{ name, description }] }`.
4. Both commands return exit code 0 on success and non-zero on error (e.g. unknown resource, malformed file).
5. Add unit/integration tests covering: list all sequences, list all stacks, search filter, JSON output for both resources.
6. Update `docs/guides/gamedev-workflow-example.md` to replace any `ls`/`find` preset listing references with `toneforge list sequences` and `toneforge list stacks` examples.
7. Ensure no generated audio is committed and only presets/docs/tests/source code are changed.

# Constraints

- Reuse existing `list` command machinery and patterns (`src/cli/commands/list.ts`).
- `--search` and `--json` flags consistent with `toneforge list recipes` semantics.
- Do not add `--category` or `--tags` filters — sequences and stacks have different metadata schemas.
- Human-readable table output should show: preset name and description (no tags/category columns).

# Existing state

- `toneforge list [resource]` accepts `recipes` as the only valid resource type, implemented in `src/cli/commands/list.ts`.
- Sequences are JSON files under `presets/sequences/` with `name`, `description`, `events`, etc.
- Stacks are JSON files under `presets/stacks/` with `name`, `description`, `layers`, etc.

# Desired change

Extend the `list` command to accept `sequences` and `stacks` as resource values, implement file discovery for each directory, and render results in table or JSON format.

# Key Files

- `src/cli/commands/list.ts` — Extend resource validation and add `sequences`/`stacks` handlers
- `src/cli.yargs.integration.test.ts` — Add integration tests for the new resource types
- `docs/guides/gamedev-workflow-example.md` — Update preset discovery examples

# Related work

- **CLI List Recipes Command (TF-0MLYAN81319GEVJ8)** — Original list command implementation
- **Add filtering to list recipes command (TF-0MM7ENNL90AHWC0N)** — `--search`/`--category`/`--tags` filtering
- **Add JSON output to list command (TF-0MLYUBZZP1HR08I8)** — JSON output pattern
- **CLI Wiring and Integration Tests (TF-0MM8NIVXP0QH2CJB)** — Integration test patterns

# Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption**: Sequence/stack JSON files always contain a `name` field — validated at parse time.
- **Risk**: A malformed JSON preset file could crash the list command — handle parse errors gracefully (skip with warning or fail with error).
- **Scope creep**: Adding `--category` or `--tags` filters for sequences/stacks is out of scope — these resource types don't have those fields.
- **Assumption**: The `presets/sequences/` and `presets/stacks/` directories are stable and won't move.

# Appendix

No interview conducted — the work item description was sufficiently detailed to proceed directly to the brief draft.

## Summary

Convert ToneForge's ~53 hard-coded TypeScript recipe factories into declarative, file-backed ToneGraph configs (JSON/YAML) so recipes can be discovered, loaded, played, exported, and versioned from disk at runtime — while preserving backward compatibility with existing code-based recipes and deterministic rendering.

## Architecture Decision: Unified buildOfflineGraph Backend

Analysis confirmed that Tone.js is not used in any production code path. The CLI, TUI, stack/sequence renderers, analyze, classify, explore, and library modules all render exclusively through `buildOfflineGraph` using standard Web Audio API on `node-web-audio-api`. The 53 Tone.js recipe factory files exist but are never loaded — no CLI code path calls `resolveFactory()`. The web demo is the sole Tone.js consumer and can be migrated to use `buildOfflineGraph` + the browser's native `OfflineAudioContext` (the `buildOfflineGraph` functions use only standard W3C Web Audio API methods that work identically in Node.js and browsers).

**Decision**: Remove Tone.js entirely (tracked in child work item TF-0MN06817414DW638) and build ToneGraph targeting only the `buildOfflineGraph` / standard Web Audio API path. This eliminates the dual-mode loader problem, the dual-implementation maintenance burden, and a large unused dependency.

ToneGraph configs will target a single backend: standard Web Audio API graph construction on an `OfflineAudioContext` (or `AudioContext` for real-time playback). The loader will receive a `BaseAudioContext` as a parameter and build nodes using `ctx.createOscillator()`, `ctx.createGain()`, etc. — the same pattern used by all 53 existing `buildOfflineGraph` functions.

## Problem Statement

Today every recipe is a hand-written TypeScript module with a `buildOfflineGraph` function that constructs a raw Web Audio API graph. Adding or tweaking a recipe requires editing TypeScript, rebuilding, and redeploying. There is no way for end-users or non-developers to author, share, or version recipes independently of the codebase.

## User Stories

- As a **sound designer**, I want to author recipes as YAML/JSON files so I can iterate on sound design without writing TypeScript or rebuilding the project.
- As a **developer**, I want a declarative graph format so I can programmatically generate and validate recipes.
- As a **contributor**, I want file-backed recipes discovered automatically at runtime so I can drop a file into `presets/recipes/` and have it appear in listings.
- As an **operator**, I want existing code-based recipes to continue working unchanged so there is zero regression risk during migration.

## Existing State (PoC — commit 3f6c4ed on main)

A proof-of-concept has been committed with the following components:

### src/core/tonegraph.ts (184 lines)
Minimal ToneGraph loader. Exports `loadToneGraph(graph, opts)` returning `ToneGraphHandle`. Currently targets Tone.js — this will need to be rewritten to target standard Web Audio API instead.

**Issues identified:**
- Targets Tone.js (now confirmed as the wrong backend — should target Web Audio API)
- Uses `any` types extensively — no typed schema for the graph document
- Only supports flat `routing` as `{from, to}` pairs — no `chain()` shorthand, no bus routing
- No sequence/transport/automation support
- No RNG integration (accepts `rng` in options but never uses it)
- No namespace (`ns/<namespace>/<name>`) resolution
- `start()` iterates ALL nodes indiscriminately — fragile
- Duration heuristic is basic (sum attack+decay from AmplitudeEnvelope nodes only)
- Error handling swallows all errors silently
- `createRecipeFactoryFromGraph` is dead code that always throws

### src/core/recipe.ts — discoverFileBackedRecipes() (lines 455-565)
Scans `presets/recipes/` for .json/.yaml/.yml files and registers them as lazy recipe entries.

**Issues identified:**
- Imports `fs`, `path`, `yaml`, and `loadToneGraph` at module top level — Node.js-only, breaks browser contexts
- `buildOfflineGraph` throws "not implemented" — file-backed recipes cannot render offline (the primary render path)
- `getParams` returns `{}` — no parameter extraction from graph
- Mixed ESM/CJS (`require("tone")` in one path)

### presets/recipes/ directory
Created but empty — no recipe files migrated yet.

## Architecture Constraints

### Single Backend: Standard Web Audio API
After removing Tone.js (TF-0MN06817414DW638), all rendering uses `buildOfflineGraph(rng, ctx, duration)` where `ctx` is a `BaseAudioContext` (`OfflineAudioContext` for offline rendering, `AudioContext` for real-time playback). The ToneGraph loader must target this same API surface.

### Determinism
Rendering is deterministic: seed 42 rendered 10 times produces byte-identical output (`src/core/renderer.test.ts`). File-backed recipes must maintain this guarantee.

### Recipe Params Separation
Recipe params are extracted via separate `*-params.ts` files with zero heavy dependencies. ToneGraph configs should declare params in a way that avoids importing audio libraries for param extraction.

## DSP Primitives Required

From reviewing all 53+ recipes, the ToneGraph loader must support:
- **Oscillators**: sine, sawtooth, square, triangle with frequency automation (sweeps, ramps)
- **Noise**: white noise (RNG-filled buffers), brown noise (leaky integrator), pink noise approximation
- **Filters**: lowpass, highpass, bandpass with Q control and LFO modulation
- **Envelopes**: attack/decay, ADSR, multi-stage (attack, sustain-decay, tail-decay)
- **FM synthesis**: carrier + modulator with modulation index/depth gain
- **Gain nodes**: level control, per-layer mixing
- **Sample playback**: `loadSample()` for CC0 samples with looping
- **Parameter automation**: `setValueAtTime`, `linearRampToValueAtTime`, LFO via stepped `setValueAtTime`
- **Multi-layer composition**: multiple parallel signal paths mixed to destination

## ToneGraph v0.1 Spec (from design conversation — not yet written to disk)

Top-level fields: `version`, `engine`, `meta`, `random`, `transport`, `nodes`, `routing`, `sequences`, `namespaces`.

Loader responsibilities:
1. Init RNG from `graph.random` (seed, algorithm)
2. Create Web Audio API nodes from `nodes` map (keyed by name, typed by `kind`)
3. Build routing from `routing` (connection pairs, chain shorthand, bus routing)
4. Build sequences from `sequences` (timed events, loops, callbacks)
5. Apply parameter automation
6. Return a handle with `start()`, `stop()`, `dispose()`, duration info

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Prerequisite**: Tone.js removal (TF-0MN06817414DW638) is completed first
2. **ToneGraph Schema**: A typed TypeScript interface/type for the ToneGraph v0.1 document format, validated at load time
3. **Web Audio API Loader**: `loadToneGraph(graph, ctx, rng)` builds a standard Web Audio API graph on any `BaseAudioContext`
4. **JSON & YAML Support**: ToneGraph files in both formats are discovered from `presets/recipes/` and registered in the recipe registry
5. **Deterministic RNG**: `graph.random` seeds are used to initialize the seeded RNG; identical seeds produce identical output
6. **Node Coverage**: Loader supports all DSP primitives listed above
7. **Routing**: Supports flat `{from, to}` pairs, `chain()` shorthand, and bus routing
8. **Sequences & Automation**: Loader builds sequences and applies parameter automation per spec
9. **Namespace Resolution**: `ns/<namespace>/<name>` node references resolved via registry
11. **Offline Rendering Parity**: At least one migrated recipe (ui-scifi-confirm) renders byte-identical output compared to its TypeScript `buildOfflineGraph` implementation at seed 42
12. **Parameter Extraction**: File-backed recipes expose `getParams()` without importing audio libraries
13. **No Browser Breakage**: Core recipe module does not import Node.js-only modules at top level
14. **Unit Tests**: Loader behavior covered by unit tests
16. **Spec Document**: ToneGraph v0.1 spec written to `docs/tonegraph.md` with format reference and examples
17. **Clean Build**: TypeScript compiles without errors; all pre-existing tests continue to pass

## Risks & Assumptions

### Risks
- **Medium**: The full DSP primitive set (especially FM synthesis, noise generation, sample playback) is large; covering all 53 recipes is an epic-scale effort
- **Medium**: Envelope implementation — Tone.js `AmplitudeEnvelope` has no direct Web Audio API equivalent; the existing `buildOfflineGraph` functions implement envelopes manually via gain node automation, and ToneGraph must do the same
- **Low**: YAML parsing dependency (`js-yaml`) is already in package.json

### Assumptions
- Tone.js removal (TF-0MN06817414DW638) is completed before ToneGraph loader work begins
- The ToneGraph v0.1 spec (from design conversation) is the authoritative format definition
- Migration of all 53 recipes is the long-term goal but not required for initial delivery — one PoC recipe (ui-scifi-confirm) is sufficient for v0.1
- Existing code-based recipes will coexist with file-backed recipes indefinitely (no forced migration)

# Web-Based Single-Sound Editor (Embeddable)

## Problem statement

ToneForge's parameter editing is currently command-flag based (CLI) or wizard-driven (TUI). Designers in the AI_Hell Enemy Gym need a **spatial, tactile editor** for shaping a single sound's parameters in-context — sliders, rotary dials, and XY touchpads — with live auditioning. The editor must be embeddable in host views (first target: Enemy Gym) without adopting ToneForge's build stack.

## Users

- **Primary: game sound/level designer** (AI_Hell Enemy Gym) — attach a sound to an enemy, shape it via direct-manipulation controls with immediate audio feedback, while tuning other enemy settings.
- **Secondary: game/app developer or prototyper** — quick visual way to dial in a placeholder sound and capture resulting parameters/seed.
- **Tertiary: sound designer** — shared, reproducible representation (seed + parameter overrides / preset) for handoff.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Browser editor with controls** — Loads a single sound (recipe + seed), renders its parameters as controls including at least sliders, rotary dials, and an XY touchpad.
2. **Live update & audition** — Every control updates the sound; a preview control plays, stops, and loops with changes reflected on the next render.
3. **Deterministic serialisation** — Editor state serialises to versioned `SoundPreset` JSON (`recipe`, `seed`, `overrides`); reloading reproduces the sound, verified byte-identically by automated test.
4. **WAV export** — Edited sound exports to WAV through the existing ToneForge pipeline.
5. **Embeddable mount / clean dispose** — Mounts into a host container via documented API; unmount test asserts no leaked listeners/timers/audio nodes or new globals.
6. **Theming & graceful degradation** — Adapts to container size, themable (background/foreground/accent), degrades safely when Web Audio requires a gesture.
7. **Demo & integration documentation** — Reference/demo page for standalone use; documented adapter for Enemy-Gym-style plain-DOM embedding with AI_Hell mapping.
8. **Accessibility** — All controls labelled, keyboard-operable, units/ranges exposed; ARIA/focus order documented.
9. **Tests & build gates** — Unit tests (parameter model, serialisation round-trip, widget clamping) + ≥1 browser/e2e test; `npm test` and `npx tsc --noEmit` pass.

## Constraints

- **Single-sound scope only** — no stacking/sequencing/mixing UI.
- **Embeddable by design** — no host routing, no global CSS, no framework dependency.
- **Reuse existing modules** — no duplication of synthesis or analysis logic.
- **Determinism** — same serialised preset → byte-identical output.
- **Autoplay policy** — explicit user gesture required to start audio.

## Out of scope

- Multi-sound / stack / sequence / mixer editing UI.
- Replacing `../AI_Hell/src/audio/effects.ts` or performing the AI_Hell migration (tracked in AH-0MUTUOB7X007PR9J).
- Server-side rendering service.
- Real-time collaborative editing.
- Full accessibility implementation (documented only; ARIA patterns sufficient, full WCAG compliance deferred).

## Suggested approach

1. **Component boundary** — framework-agnostic custom element / micro-frontend entry with documented mount API (`mount(container)`, `dispose()`, `onChange(preset)`).
2. **Parameter model** — derive editable control set from each recipe's seed-derived parameter module (`src/recipes/*-params.ts`); define `SoundPreset` schema `{ recipe, seed, overrides: Record<string, number> }`.
3. **Synthesis/render** — reuse offline render path (`renderRecipe` / `buildOfflineGraph`) for deterministic rendering; Web Audio API for real-time preview. Note: TF-0MN06817414DW638 may remove Tone.js dependency.
4. **Controls** — widget kit (range slider, rotary dial, XY pad, toggle/select) with typed min/max/step/units; parameter-to-control mapping data-driven.
5. **Host integration** — thin adapter + reference demo page; document Enemy Gym mounting pattern.
6. **Persistence/export** — save/load named presets; export WAV via existing pipeline.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Tone.js deprecation** (TF-0MN06817414DW638) may change the synthesis substrate; design should favour `buildOfflineGraph` / vanilla Web Audio API where feasible.
- **AI_Hell integration dependency** — embedding in Enemy Gym is blocked until AH-0MUTUOB7X007PR9J (Switch game audio to ToneForge) is complete.
- **Cross-browser Web Audio** — autoplay policy enforcement and Web Audio API support may differ; graceful degradation is a requirement.
- **Scope creep** — "single-sound" boundary must be maintained; multi-sound requests should be captured as separate work items.
- **Assumption**: existing ToneForge web infrastructure (Vite, `web/` directory) is available and functional as a build substrate.
- **Assumption**: recipe parameter definitions in `src/recipes/*-params.ts` are stable and comprehensive enough to drive the control set.

## Summary

Make the shared render path preset-aware: given a `SoundPreset` (recipe + seed + overrides), render the sound deterministically in the browser via the cross-platform audio abstraction, with overrides replacing seed-derived parameter values. Reuse the existing `buildOfflineGraph`/recipe registry — no duplicated synthesis logic. This is the highest-risk item because today `buildOfflineGraph(rng, ctx, duration)` derives parameters internally and exposes no injection point.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `renderPreset(preset)` entry point returns the same `RenderResult` shape as `renderRecipe` and applies every override in the preset to the rendered audio.
- Determinism: rendering the same `SoundPreset` twice yields byte-identical `Float32Array` samples; changing an override yields *different* samples for at least one representative recipe (both asserted by test).
- Every registered recipe (built-in and file-backed) honours overrides for all of its declared parameters, verified by a registry-wide test that iterates `registry.list()` and asserts an override changes the output.
- Rendering uses the cross-platform Web Audio abstraction (native `OfflineAudioContext` in the browser, `node-web-audio-api` in Node) and imports no Node-only audio module on the browser path.
- Baseline behaviour is unchanged: with no overrides, `renderPreset({recipe, seed, overrides:{}})` is byte-identical to `renderRecipe(recipe, seed)`.
- `npm test` and `npx tsc --noEmit` pass.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add a small `applyOverrides(params, overrides)` helper and thread an optional `overrides` argument through the render path and `RecipeRegistration.buildOfflineGraph` (or an equivalent params-injection hook) — decide the exact seam during the prototype below.
- Refactor built-in recipe graph builders to merge `getParams(rng)` with `overrides`; extend the file-backed registration's existing param-injection to apply overrides.
- Add `renderPreset(preset, duration?)` alongside `renderRecipe` reusing `renderer.ts`; do not fork synthesis.
- Build on the browser-compatible abstraction from TF-0MUUB39EL000YCT0 (cross-platform `OfflineAudioContext`/`AudioContext`).

## Prototype / Experiment

Prototype the override seam on 2–3 representative recipes (oscillator, noise/filter, file-backed) before touching all recipes. Success threshold: the representative set renders deterministically and an override demonstrably changes output; then roll the seam out registry-wide behind the registry-wide coverage test.
